35.0.0.en: In the days of Jehoiakim king of Judah there were raids by the Babylonians on Judea, which made the inhabitants of the villages and the open country take refuge in Jerusalem to shelter inside its walls. Among them were the Rechabites, who lived in tents in Judea near Jerusalem.

35.1.0.en: The Rechabites: they are one of the tribes of the Kenites, and of Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, who accompanied the Jews to the Promised Land and were influenced by the character and conduct of the Jews.

35.1.1.en: The chambers: the side rooms of the temple of the Lord.

35.1.2.en: God commanded Jeremiah to bring a group of the Rechabites who lived in tents inside Jerusalem, and to bring them into one of the chambers of the house of the Lord and offer them wine to drink.

35.2.0.en: Jeremiah took one of the leaders of the Rechabites, who was called “Jaazaniah,” and his household and those of the Rechabites who were with him, and brought them into the chamber of the sons of Hanan in the house of the Lord.

35.3.2.en: Jeremiah offered them wine in large vessels and cups so that they might fill them and drink as they wished.

35.4.0.en: Jonadab the son of Rechab: he is the father of the Rechabites. He lived in the days of the prophet Elijah, that is, about two and a half centuries before the time of Jeremiah.

35.4.1.en: The Rechabites refused to drink wine because their ancestor Jonadab had commanded them not to drink wine forever, that is, never to drink at all, because wine represents the pleasures of the world.

35.5.0.en: Jonadab also commanded them to live as strangers to the world, by the following:

35.5.2.en: 2- Not owning fields and gardens to plant with vineyards and olives.

35.5.3.en: And this is in addition to not drinking wine, which is the third proof of their estrangement from the world.

35.6.0.en: The Rechabites declared their obedience throughout their lives to their father Jonadab in not drinking wine, living in tents, and not owning lands to cultivate.

35.7.0.en: When the armies of the Babylonians moved and attacked Judea, the sons of Rechab took refuge in Jerusalem to shelter in it.

35.7.1.en: If the sons of Rechab became strangers to the world in obedience to their father “Jonadab the son of Rechab,” how much more should we become strangers to the material things of the world and its lusts out of our love for God. May we use everything in measure and not cling to food, clothing or possessions.

35.8.0.en: God sent Jeremiah to the men of Judah to rebuke them for not accepting God's discipline for their sins at the hand of the Babylonians.

35.9.0.en: God rebuked His people for not obeying His commandments, while the sons of Rechab obeyed their father in not drinking wine.

35.10.0.en: He also rebuked them for rejecting the words of the earlier prophets since the days of Moses, and the later ones such as Jeremiah, that they should not worship idols and should turn back from their evil lusts so as to dwell in the land of Canaan. They did not obey, so they deserved the divine discipline, which is the captivity and expulsion from their land.

35.11.0.en: By this the sons of Rechab were distinguished from the people of God, the children of Israel; that is, the Gentiles from the Jews.

35.11.1.en: Obedience to God's commandments protects you from many troubles, so do not make light of it, and if you have violated them, return quickly to God with repentance.

35.12.0.en: Because of the disobedience of God's people to Him, He will punish them with the captivity, and He declares His name the LORD of hosts, that is, the Lord of power, that they might fear Him, perhaps repenting at the last moment.

36.0.0.en: He specifies the time of the prophecy, which is the fourth year of King Jehoiakim of Judah, that is, the year 605 BC. This king was wicked and hated Jeremiah because he proclaimed the voice of God.

36.1.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah to write all the prophecies that God had given him, from the days of King Josiah, that is, the year 626 BC, until the time of the writing of the prophecies, that is, 605 BC, a period of 21 years. They include prophecies against the kingdom of Israel, the kingdom of Judah and the other nations. Perhaps the motive for this was the nearness of the time of the captivity and Jeremiah's exposure to being kept away from the temple or imprisoned, which would hinder God's word from reaching the people. So God commanded him to write the prophecies so that they would be preserved, to be carried by the captives to Babylon or by the fugitives to Egypt, or so that a copy of them would remain in Jerusalem for them to read and repent.

36.2.0.en: God's purpose in these prophecies and in their writing is to move the hearts of His people to repent, so that He turns back from their punishment and saves them.

36.3.0.en: The roll of a book: thin sheets of skin or papyrus on which one writes, which are rolled up when kept, and when read these rolled-up sheets are opened.

36.3.1.en: Jeremiah called his disciple, the prophet Baruch, to write for him the prophecies that he would dictate to him. Jeremiah kept them in memory by the power of the Holy Spirit, or he may have written down each prophecy after proclaiming it. So he wrote all the prophecies of Jeremiah on a roll.

36.4.0.en: Jeremiah was forbidden to approach the temple. This is the meaning of the word “shut up,” and it does not mean that he was shut up in a prison, as is shown by the fact that he was able to flee, as v. 19 makes clear. This was in the year 605 BC, at the time when Babylon defeated Egypt in the battle of Carchemish on the river Euphrates and then began to advance toward Palestine to besiege Jerusalem.

36.5.0.en: Jeremiah commanded his disciple, the prophet Baruch, the recorder of his prophecies, that after writing all his prophecies he should read them in the hearing of the people gathered in the house of the Lord, those living in Jerusalem and also those coming from the land of Judah to the house of the Lord. This happened in the ninth month of the year 604 BC, that is, the fifth year of King Jehoiakim, so there is a time gap between the time of the writing of the roll and the time of its reading, of more than a year. This was on the day of the public fast.

36.5.2.en: 8- And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the LORD in the LORD'S house. 9- And it came to pass in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before the LORD to all the people in Jerusalem, and to all the people that came from the cities of Judah unto Jerusalem.

36.5.3.en: 10- Then read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the LORD'S house, in the ears of all the people.

36.6.0.en: Baruch is a Hebrew name meaning blessed. He was a disciple of Jeremiah and recorded his prophecies for him. After this he went to Babylon and wrote a book of his own, which is one of the deuterocanonical books, that is, within the Holy Bible, but the Protestants removed it. He was related to Jeremiah by kinship.

36.6.1.en: The writing of the prophecies took more than a year, and then Baruch read them in the house of the Lord before the people.

36.7.0.en: In the ninth month of the ninth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, which corresponds to the year 604 BC in the month of December, that is, in winter, they proclaimed in Jerusalem a public fast for all the people. It is not one of the religious fasts written in the Law of Moses, but a fast because of the approach of the armies of Babylon to Jerusalem and the sense of danger, so they sought God to deliver them. Sadly this fast was not accompanied by a turning back from their sins.

36.8.0.en: Gemariah the son of Shaphan: Shaphan was the scribe of King Josiah (2 Kgs 22:3, 8), and his son Gemariah was also the brother of Ahikam, who treated Jeremiah gently (ch. 25:24). Baruch went to the temple and went up to one of the chambers of the temple, the one belonging to Gemariah the son of Shaphan, who sympathized with Jeremiah. He stood and looked out from above from one of the windows of the chamber on the people gathered in the court of the temple and read the prophecies of Jeremiah that he had recorded for him. It appears that they were written in a condensed form, so that all of it could be read in a reasonable time to all the people.

36.8.1.en: Fasting is an opportunity to offer your love to God by giving up your material attachments, but it must be joined with your repentance, so that it is a pure fast with which God is pleased, and you feel spiritual consolations and blessing in your life.

36.8.2.en: [3] The reading of the book to the princes (vv. 11-19)

36.8.3.en: 11- When Michaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, had heard out of the book all the words of the LORD, 12- Then he went down into the king's house, into the scribe's chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there, even Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes. 13- Then Michaiah declared unto them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people. 14- Therefore all the princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, unto Baruch, saying, Take in thine hand the roll wherein thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come. So Baruch the son of Neriah took the roll in his hand, and came unto them. 15- And they said unto him, Sit down now, and read it in our ears. So Baruch read it in their ears. 16- Now it came to pass, when they had heard all the words, they were afraid both one and other, and said unto Baruch, We will surely tell the king of all these words. 17- And they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now, How didst thou write all these words at his mouth?

36.8.4.en: 18- Then Baruch answered them, He pronounced all these words unto me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ink in the book.

36.8.5.en: 19- Then said the princes unto Baruch, Go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and let no man know where ye be.

36.9.0.en: Among those gathered in the court of the temple who heard Baruch's reading of the roll was a young man, Michaiah the son of Gemariah, one of the leaders of the people, whose grandfather was Shaphan, who had been the official scribe of King Josiah.

36.10.0.en: After hearing the prophecies of Jeremiah from the mouth of Baruch, Michaiah hurried to the royal palace, and there in one of the rooms called the scribe's chamber, where the scribes of the king and the princes used to meet, he found a number of princes, among them his father Gemariah. Michaiah knew from his father Gemariah the place where they met.

36.11.0.en: Michaiah told the princes of the prophecies of Jeremiah that he had heard from Baruch, and it appears that he was afraid because of the power of the words. This shows that he was a spiritual young man who cared for the word of God and was affected by it.

36.12.0.en: The princes sent a representative of theirs named Jehudi to Baruch, and asked him to come to them with the roll. Baruch obeyed and went to them in the royal palace.

36.13.0.en: The princes asked Baruch to read the book to them, and he read it before them.

36.14.0.en: When the leaders of the people heard Jeremiah's prophecies and God's threats to punish His people, they were very afraid and felt their responsibility to inform the king so that he would move the whole people in the way of repentance. From this we understand that the fear of God was in the hearts of these leaders, while the king, on the contrary, was wicked and did not fear God.

36.15.0.en: The princes asked Baruch how all these prophecies had been written and gathered from the days of King Josiah until the time of Jehoiakim, that is, a period of 21 years, as we mentioned.

36.16.0.en: Baruch informed them that the prophet Jeremiah dictated the prophecies to him and he wrote them in the book.

36.17.0.en: The princes advised Baruch to flee, he and Jeremiah, and hide in an unknown place, because they feared for them from the vengeance of the king and the false prophets. This confirms their love for Jeremiah and Baruch and their fear of God.

36.17.1.en: The fear of God makes a person care about hearing His word and even obeying it, so he tries to carry out His commandments and, out of his love for God, warns others so that they turn back from their sins. So be strong and be ready every day, setting your only goal as eternal life and remembering also the judgment.

36.18.0.en: The princes took the roll that Baruch had written and put it in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, who was probably the official scribe of the king. Then they went in to the king and told him what Baruch had done in the house of the Lord and that the roll was in the king's palace in the chamber of Elishama. Elishama was probably with them.

36.19.0.en: The king probably received this news coldly, and sent one of his aides in the palace, Jehudi, whom the princes had sent earlier, to bring Baruch from the temple (v. 15). Jehudi brought it from the chamber of Elishama and came with it to the king, and read it before him and before the princes standing with him.

36.20.0.en: The winter house: a house prepared for dwelling in winter, characterized by warmth. This confirms that this matter was in December of the year 604 BC, as we mentioned.

36.20.1.en: The hearth: a stove that was used for heating or cooking in ancient times and until recently in the twentieth century. Some wood is lit in it, giving a fire for warmth within a small space surrounded by bricks or stones.

36.20.2.en: Here He confirms the time of the reading of the book, which was in the ninth month, corresponding to December, that is, in winter, and the hearth was burning for warmth in the king's room.

36.20.3.en: Penknife: a small knife used by the scribe in preparing the wooden pen so that it has a fine point with which to write when it is dipped in ink.

36.21.0.en: Instead of the king fearing God's anger, he dared to command that the roll be torn with the scribe's penknife, and he could not bear to hear God's word except a few lines of it. He should rather have feared God, torn his clothes and wept over his sins, and God would have had mercy on him and on his people.

36.22.0.en: The king's stubbornness was so great that he did not listen to the entreaties of his princes not to burn God's word contained in the roll.

36.23.0.en: King Jehoiakim persisted in his evil and commanded one of his relatives, Jerahmeel the son of the king, that is, of his family, and two others of his aides, to seize Jeremiah and Baruch in order to punish them or kill them.

36.23.1.en: Do not rush in your anger, doing disturbing things and angering God and those around you. Be long-suffering and listen to the counsel of those around you, and lift your heart in prayer, and you will find your salvation and escape many evils.

36.23.2.en: [5] The second copy of the scroll (vv. 27-32)

36.23.3.en: 27- Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, after that the king had burned the roll, and the words which Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah, saying, 28- Take thee again another roll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first roll, which Jehoiakim the king of Judah hath burned. 29- And thou shalt say to Jehoiakim king of Judah, Thus saith the LORD; Thou hast burned this roll, saying, Why hast thou written therein, saying, The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land, and shall cause to cease from thence man and beast? 30- Therefore thus saith the LORD of Jehoiakim king of Judah; He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost. 31- And I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them; but they hearkened not. 32- Then took Jeremiah another roll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah; who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire: and there were added besides unto them many like words.

36.24.0.en: After King Jehoiakim burned the roll, after a period that may have been a few months, God commanded Jeremiah to prepare a new roll and write in it all the prophecies previously written in the first roll. This shows the inclination of God and His children toward positive action, which is recording the word of God, and not thinking about the evil of the wicked, that is, the evil of Jehoiakim and those with him.

36.25.0.en: God sent King Jehoiakim a message by the tongue of Jeremiah, whether he wrote it in the roll or sent it with someone, in which God rebukes Jehoiakim because he refused to listen to God's punishment, namely the coming of the king of Babylon to Jerusalem and his taking it and destroying it and destroying men and animals, and he showed his stubbornness toward God in his burning of the roll.

36.26.0.en: God sent Jehoiakim a threat of punishment as a result of his sins, which includes two matters:

36.26.1.en: 1- None of his sons will reign over the kingdom of Judah, as is the custom with his fathers, but his son Jehoiachin will reign for a few months, and then his uncle Zedekiah.

36.26.2.en: 2- Jehoiakim will be killed at the hand of the Babylonians and his corpse thrown on the ground, and no one will bury him with honor like the rest of the kings, as a declaration of God's anger against him.

36.27.0.en: And God confirms the words of the roll, that He will punish Jerusalem and its inhabitants and the offspring of King Jehoiakim for their many evils.

36.28.0.en: Jeremiah obeyed and brought a roll and dictated to Baruch the prophecies previously written in the first roll, and added some further details of the prophecies, among them God's word about His punishment of Jehoiakim mentioned in (vv. 30, 31). Thus God preserved His word however much the wicked tried to remove it, for whoever stands before God or tries to remove His word, God of course laughs at him.

36.28.1.en: Obey God's word even if it is hard, and keep away from sin however attractive it is, and do not try to interpret God's word according to your desires, for then God will have mercy on you.
